what: NNN REIT owns about 3,600 single-tenant retail properties across America and leases them on long triple-net leases to convenience stores, car washes, restaurants and automotive service chains.
customers: Retail and service chains that prefer to lease rather than own their buildings.
money: net lease rent from retail properties
interest and gains on property sales
moat: Long leases with built-in rent increases on properties leased to tenants whose business depends on that specific location, which makes renewal rates very high.
risks: Many tenants are smaller chains without investment-grade credit
19 times earnings for low single digit rent growth
Rising interest rates raise the cost of the capital needed to buy more properties
opportunities: A 42.1% net margin and $675M of free cash flow on $973M of revenue
Only $348M of debt at the corporate level, unusually low for a net lease REIT
The dividend has been raised for 36 consecutive years, a record few companies match
watch: Occupancy and the yield on newly acquired properties.
